title: Recent Trends in Physics — 40 MCQs
description: Covers surface waves (Rayleigh and Love), internal seismic waves (P and S), wave patterns of the 2015 Gorkha earthquake, gravitational waves, nanotechnology and the Higgs boson.

questions.q: P-waves are
questions.explanation: P-waves (primary waves) are longitudinal waves that travel by compression and rarefaction of the medium.

questions.q: S-waves are
options: surface waves that travel through liquids
questions.explanation: S-waves (secondary waves) are transverse waves in which particle motion is perpendicular to the direction of propagation.

questions.q: Love waves are a type of
options: surface wave with horizontal transverse motion
questions.explanation: Love waves are surface waves that cause horizontal shearing of the ground perpendicular to the direction of travel.

questions.q: Rayleigh waves are surface waves that cause
options: elliptical particle motion in the vertical plane
questions.explanation: Rayleigh waves produce a retrograde elliptical motion of ground particles in the plane of propagation.

questions.q: Which seismic waves cannot travel through the liquid outer core?
questions.explanation: S-waves are shear waves and cannot propagate through fluids; they are absent beyond the core-mantle boundary.

questions.q: The 2015 Gorkha earthquake occurred in
questions.explanation: The Gorkha earthquake of 25 April 2015 struck central Nepal with its epicentre near Gorkha district.

questions.q: Gravitational waves are
options: ripples in spacetime caused by accelerating masses
questions.explanation: Gravitational waves are propagating distortions of spacetime predicted by general relativity and produced by accelerating masses.

questions.q: Nanotechnology deals with structures whose size is typically in the range
questions.explanation: Nanotechnology involves materials and devices with at least one dimension between approximately 1 and 100 nanometres.

questions.q: The Higgs boson is associated with
options: the mechanism that gives mass to elementary particles
questions.explanation: The Higgs field and its associated boson explain how particles acquire mass through the Higgs mechanism.

questions.q: The first direct detection of gravitational waves was announced by
questions.explanation: LIGO (Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory) detected GW150914 in 2015 and announced it in 2016.

questions.q: P-waves travel faster than S-waves because
options: the bulk modulus contributes in addition to the shear modulus
they travel only on the surface
questions.explanation: The speed of P-waves depends on both bulk and shear moduli, while S-wave speed depends only on the shear modulus, making P-waves faster.

questions.q: The approximate magnitude of the 2015 Gorkha earthquake was
questions.explanation: The main shock of the Gorkha earthquake was measured at moment magnitude Mw 7.8.

questions.q: Love waves travel
options: along the Earth’s surface with horizontal particle motion
questions.explanation: Love waves are trapped near the surface and produce side-to-side horizontal shaking.

questions.q: Rayleigh waves are often the most destructive in an earthquake because
options: they produce both vertical and horizontal ground motion of large amplitude
questions.explanation: Rayleigh waves arrive later, have large amplitudes and cause complex rolling motion that damages structures.

questions.q: The Higgs boson was discovered at
options: the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN
questions.explanation: The ATLAS and CMS experiments at the LHC announced the discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012.

questions.q: Gravitational waves travel at the speed of
questions.explanation: According to general relativity, gravitational waves propagate at the speed of light c.

questions.q: One nanometre is equal to
questions.explanation: 1 nm = 10⁻⁹ m.

questions.q: The shadow zone for S-waves is larger than that for P-waves because
options: S-waves are absorbed completely by the liquid outer core
S-waves travel only on the surface
questions.explanation: S-waves cannot pass through the liquid outer core, creating a wide shadow zone; P-waves can travel through the core but are refracted.

questions.q: The 2015 Gorkha earthquake was caused primarily by
options: thrust faulting on the Main Himalayan Thrust
questions.explanation: The earthquake resulted from the ongoing collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates along the Main Himalayan Thrust.

questions.q: Nanoparticles exhibit properties different from bulk material mainly because of
options: increased surface-to-volume ratio and quantum effects
questions.explanation: At the nanoscale a large fraction of atoms lie on the surface and quantum confinement becomes significant, altering physical and chemical behaviour.

questions.q: The mass of the Higgs boson is approximately
questions.explanation: The Higgs boson mass measured at the LHC is about 125 GeV/c².

questions.q: Which type of seismic wave arrives first at a recording station?
questions.explanation: P-waves are the fastest and therefore the first to be recorded on a seismogram.

questions.q: Gravitational waves were first detected from the merger of
options: a black hole and a star
questions.explanation: GW150914 originated from the coalescence of two stellar-mass black holes.

questions.q: Love waves require a
options: layered structure with a low-velocity surface layer
questions.explanation: Love waves are guided by a low-speed surface layer overlying a higher-speed substrate.

questions.q: The unit “nanometre” is most relevant to
questions.explanation: Atomic radii and nanostructures are measured on the nanometre scale.

questions.q: If the speed of P-waves in a rock is 6 km s⁻¹ and the speed of S-waves is 3.5 km s⁻¹, the time difference for a station 70 km from the epicentre is approximately
The epicentre of the 2015 Gorkha earthquake was located approximately
questions.explanation: The epicentre was near Barpak in Gorkha district, about 80 km northwest of Kathmandu.

questions.q: The strain sensitivity of a LIGO interferometer is of the order of
questions.explanation: LIGO measures fractional length changes of order 10⁻²¹ caused by passing gravitational waves.

questions.q: A nanoparticle has a diameter of 20 nm. Express this size in metres.
The Higgs field is non-zero in the vacuum. This fact is responsible for
options: giving mass to W and Z bosons and to fermions
the expansion of the universe only
questions.explanation: The non-zero vacuum expectation value of the Higgs field generates masses for the weak gauge bosons and, through Yukawa couplings, for fermions.

questions.q: Which statement about the 2015 Gorkha earthquake is correct?
options: It produced significant surface rupture across the Kathmandu valley
It was a deep-focus earthquake (>300 km)
It occurred on a strike-slip fault
It was caused by volcanic activity
questions.explanation: Although the main slip was buried, the earthquake caused strong ground motion and damage throughout the Kathmandu valley; surface rupture was limited but ground failure was extensive.

questions.q: The speed of Rayleigh waves is typically
options: slightly less than the speed of S-waves
greater than the speed of P-waves
equal to the speed of light
questions.explanation: Rayleigh-wave speed is approximately 0.92 times the S-wave speed in a homogeneous half-space.

questions.q: In nanotechnology the term “bottom-up” approach refers to
options: assembling structures atom by atom or molecule by molecule
carving bulk material down to nanoscale
questions.explanation: Bottom-up fabrication builds nanostructures from atomic or molecular components, in contrast to top-down lithography.

questions.q: The frequency of gravitational waves detected from binary black-hole mergers is typically in the range
questions.explanation: Stellar-mass black-hole mergers produce gravitational waves that sweep through the LIGO-sensitive band of roughly 30–300 Hz.

questions.q: P-wave shadow zones exist because
options: P-waves are refracted by the liquid outer core and solid inner core
questions.explanation: The abrupt change in velocity at the core-mantle boundary refracts P-waves, creating shadow zones between approximately 105° and 140° epicentral distance.

questions.q: The discovery of the Higgs boson completed the
questions.explanation: The Higgs boson was the last fundamental particle predicted by the Standard Model to be observed experimentally.

questions.q: A seismogram shows a clear S-wave arrival but no surface waves. The most likely explanation is that the station is
options: very close to the epicentre or the event is deep
questions.explanation: Surface waves are generated more efficiently by shallow events and grow with distance; near or deep sources may show weak or absent surface waves.

questions.q: Quantum dots used in nanotechnology are
options: semiconductor nanocrystals whose optical properties depend on size
questions.explanation: Quantum dots are nanoscale semiconductor particles that exhibit size-dependent band gaps and fluorescence.

questions.q: The energy scale of the Higgs vacuum expectation value is approximately
questions.explanation: The vacuum expectation value of the Higgs field is v ≈ 246 GeV, setting the electroweak scale.

questions.q: Which pair of waves is most responsible for the prolonged shaking felt during the 2015 Gorkha earthquake in Kathmandu?
questions.explanation: After the body waves, large-amplitude surface waves (Rayleigh and Love) caused the extended strong ground motion observed in the valley.
